subject: maths
question: In a group of 22 men, two men whose average age is 58 years are replaced by two new men. If the average age of the group decreases by 2 years, then what is the average age of two new men?
solution:
**Given:**

Number of men in the group = 22

Average age of two replaced men = 58 years

Decrease in average age of the group = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Average age = (Sum of ages) / (Number of individuals)

**Calculation:**

Let the total initial age of the group be S.

Initial average age of the group = S / 22

Sum of ages of the two men replaced = 2 × 58 = 116 years

New average age of the group = (S - 116 + Sum of ages of two new men) / 22

Given that the average age decreases by 2 years:

New average age = (S / 22) - 2

So,

(S - 116 + Sum of ages of two new men) / 22 = (S / 22) - 2

Multiplying both sides by 22:

S - 116 + Sum of ages of two new men = S - 44

⇒ Sum of ages of two new men = 116 - 44

⇒ Sum of ages of two new men = 72

Average age of two new men = 72 / 2

⇒ Average age of two new men = 36 years

**The average age of the two new men is 36 years.**
